summary: Backend testing for Payout Request system (Kurye Ödeme Talebi). Created comprehensive pytest suite (18 tests) covering credit/revert earning idempotency, balance aggregation with earning type, can-request validation (low balance / cooldown / mütabakat blocker / active percent installment), create_payout_request validation (min 1000, PDF only, balance overrun), approve flow with percent installment deduction, deduction cap to remaining, double-approve rejection, over-request rejection, company listing with status filter, fixed-installment backwards compat, and order delivered hook. All 18 pytest tests PASS plus original 2 native tests still PASS. HTTP smoke tests via public URL confirm proper auth (401 unauth) and error responses (404 for missing courier/request).

minor.issue: Endpoints only require_auth; no ownership check that the calling courier == path courier_id. A logged-in courier could query/create a payout for ANOTHER courier. Recommend adding a check that courier_id in path matches authenticated user (when role=courier).
admin_id and admin_name come from form body — not derived from the authenticated admin token. Easy to spoof / mismatched audit trail. Prefer using current_user from require_admin dependency.
If R2 upload succeeds but DB insert fails, the file is orphaned (no rollback). Consider best-effort cleanup on failure.

action_items: Optional security hardening: derive admin_id/admin_name in approve from JWT, not Form body.
Optional security hardening: courier endpoints should restrict access to the same courier (or admin only).
Optional: rollback R2 upload if subsequent DB inserts fail in create_payout_request.

Note: courier login with phone 05553337766 returned 'Geçersiz telefon veya şifre' on public URL via /api/auth/courier/login — flagging in case test credentials need refresh, but this is unrelated to payout system. Admin login works.
critical_code_review_comments: approve_payout_request: admin_id/admin_name are accepted as Form fields rather than derived from JWT — audit-trail integrity risk.
Ownership: payout-requests/courier/* endpoints accept any logged-in user (require_auth) without verifying caller==courier_id.
_check_unprocessed_collections fetches up to 20000 orders to compute distinct days — fine for now but a $group aggregation by day would scale better.
deduction is capped to remaining_amount in approve, but mismatch with expected_installment_deduction shown to courier at request time is not communicated back as a delta (UI nice-to-have).
File size of routers/payout_requests.py (~605 lines) is borderline; consider splitting helpers into a service module.
test_credentials: admin onurertas/Delivery32.. works. Courier 05553337766/123456 returned 401 on /api/auth/courier/login (unrelated to payout system).
seed_data_creation: All test data inserted with TEST_ prefix or test- UUID prefix; cleaned up by fixtures after each test (transactions, invoices, payout_requests, installment_products, orders, couriers, companies, daily_mutabakat_processed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_payout_full_pytest.py covers all payout request flows. Run with: cd /app/backend && PYTHONPATH=/app/backend pytest tests/test_payout_full_pytest.py -v --asyncio-mode=auto -o asyncio_default_test_loop_scope=session -o asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope=session. The session-scoped loop is required because motor binds to the first asyncio loop. Mocked: push_notification_service.send_push_notification (per problem statement, no real FCM/APNS).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in implementation. Earning type was correctly added to all aggregations in accounting_service.py; idempotent earning works (unique by order_id+entity_id+type=earning); revert correctly removes auto_generated earnings; percent installment deduction is computed and capped properly; cooldown via created_at >= now-24h; mutabakat blocker correctly compares delivered order days vs daily_mutabakat_processed records.
